result.summary: Document A heavily favors the Client by giving them unlimited liability, ownership of your pre-existing work, the power to change scope or terms unilaterally, and a strict global non-compete clause. Document B is a balanced freelance agreement that protects your pre-existing work, caps your liability, provides clearer payment terms, and replaces the non-compete with a limited non-solicitation clause.

differences.document_a: Includes drafts, source files and any materials the Contractor owned before this Agreement that are used in the work.
differences.document_b: Excludes materials the Contractor owned before this Agreement.
differences.impact: Document A gives away ownership of your pre-existing tools and background materials to the client. Document B ensures you keep your pre-existing materials.

quotes.text: including drafts, source files and any materials the Contractor owned before this Agreement that are used in the work
It does not include materials the Contractor owned before this Agreement

differences.document_a: Fees are set out in Schedule A. The Client may change the scope at any time without changing the Fees unless agreed in writing.
differences.document_b: Fees are GBP 12,000, payable in three equal milestones. Changes to scope must be agreed in writing by both parties, including any change to the Fees.
differences.impact: Document A allows the client to force extra work on you without increasing pay. Document B specifies a fixed fee and requires mutual agreement for scope and fee changes.

quotes.text: The Client may change the scope of the Services at any time by written notice. The Fees will not change unless the Client agrees otherwise in writing
Changes to the scope of the Services must be agreed in writing by both parties, including any change to the Fees

differences.document_a: Invoices must be submitted within 14 days of completing a milestone; late invoices will not be paid. Payment is due within 90 days (or 30 days depending on conflicting clauses), and the Client may withhold payment if dissatisfied.
differences.document_b: The Client will pay the Fees within thirty (30) days of receiving a valid invoice, with interest added for late payments.
differences.impact: Document A contains contradictory payment timelines (90 days vs 30 days), forfeits payment entirely if you submit an invoice late, and allows the client to withhold money if they are unsatisfied. Document B gives a clear 30-day window and adds late payment interest.

quotes.text: Invoices must be submitted within 14 days of completing a milestone; late invoices will not be paid
The Client will pay the Fees within thirty (30) days of receiving a valid invoice

differences.document_a: All rights in the Deliverables, including any pre-existing materials of the Contractor used in them, are assigned to the Client on creation.
differences.document_b: Rights in the Deliverables pass to the Client once the Fees for them have been paid in full.
differences.impact: Document A transfers your rights immediately upon creation before you are paid. Document B ensures you retain rights until you receive full payment.

quotes.text: All rights in the Deliverables, including any pre-existing materials of the Contractor used in them, are assigned to the Client on creation
Rights in the Deliverables pass to the Client once the Fees for them have been paid in full

differences.document_a: For twenty-four (24) months after this Agreement ends, the Contractor will not provide services to any business that competes with the Client anywhere in the world.
differences.document_b: For six (6) months after this Agreement ends, the Contractor will not directly solicit the Client's customers that the Contractor worked with.
differences.impact: Document A is a severe global non-compete preventing you from working with any competitor for two years. Document B is a much milder non-solicitation restriction lasting only six months for specific clients.

quotes.text: For twenty-four (24) months after this Agreement ends, the Contractor will not provide services to any business that competes with the Client anywhere in the world
For six (6) months after this Agreement ends, the Contractor will not directly solicit the Client's customers that the Contractor worked with

differences.document_a: The Contractor is liable for all losses suffered by the Client arising from the Services, without limit, and must indemnify the Client against third-party claims.
differences.document_b: Each party's total liability under this Agreement is limited to the Fees paid in the twelve months before the claim.
differences.impact: Document A exposes you to unlimited financial ruin and third-party claims. Document B caps your total liability at the amount of fees paid over twelve months.

quotes.text: The Contractor is liable for all losses suffered by the Client arising from the Services, without limit
Each party's total liability under this Agreement is limited to the Fees paid in the twelve months before the claim

differences.document_a: The Client may terminate at any time with immediate effect, while the Contractor needs 90 days' notice. On termination the Client pays only for accepted Deliverables.
differences.document_b: Either party may terminate on thirty (30) days' written notice. On termination the Client will pay for all work performed up to the termination date.
differences.impact: Document A is heavily asymmetrical, allowing the client to fire you instantly and refuse payment for unaccepted work while locking you in for 90 days. Document B provides mutual 30-day termination and ensures payment for all performed work.

quotes.text: The Client may terminate this Agreement at any time with immediate effect. The Contractor may terminate on ninety (90) days' written notice
Either party may terminate this Agreement on thirty (30) days' written notice

differences.document_a: The Client may update these terms by posting a new version on its supplier portal. Continued work by the Contractor means acceptance.
differences.impact: Document A allows the client to secretly alter contract terms simply by updating a webpage. Document B requires both parties to agree to changes.

quotes.text: The Client may update these terms by posting a new version on its supplier portal. Continued work by the Contractor means acceptance

differences.document_a: The Contractor may not show the Deliverables in a portfolio without the Client's prior written consent.
differences.document_b: The Contractor may show the Deliverables in a portfolio after the website launches.
differences.impact: Document A blocks you from showing the work in your portfolio unless the client agrees. Document B explicitly allows you to showcase the work after launch.

quotes.text: The Contractor may not show the Deliverables in a portfolio without the Client's prior written consent
The Contractor may show the Deliverables in a portfolio after the website launches

differences.document_a: The Contractor must keep the Client's information confidential during this Agreement and for an unlimited period afterwards.
differences.document_b: The Contractor must keep the Client's information confidential during this Agreement and for three (3) years afterwards.
differences.impact: Document A imposes an indefinite confidentiality obligation. Document B limits this burden to a reasonable three-year period.

quotes.text: The Contractor must keep the Client's information confidential during this Agreement and for an unlimited period afterwards
The Contractor must keep the Client's information confidential during this Agreement and for three (3) years afterwards

differences.topic: Dispute Resolution and Class Action Waiver
differences.document_a: Any dispute will be resolved by binding arbitration in London. The Contractor waives any right to bring or join a class or collective action.
differences.document_b: The parties will try to resolve any dispute by negotiation before starting court proceedings.
differences.impact: Document A forces binding arbitration and strips you of class action rights. Document B allows for standard court proceedings after negotiation.

quotes.text: Any dispute will be resolved by binding arbitration in London. The Contractor waives any right to bring or join a class or collective action
The parties will try to resolve any dispute by negotiation before starting court proceedings

questions_for_lawyer: Are the liability caps in Document B sufficient to protect me against potential third-party claims related to the website design?
Does the non-solicitation clause in Document B leave me enough room to work with other clients in the same industry?
Does Document B protect my moral rights and ownership over background tools adequately if payment milestones are delayed?
next_steps: Refuse Document A entirely because it contains unlimited liability, unilateral term changes, and restrictive non-compete clauses.
Select Document B as your preferred baseline agreement since it provides mutual termination rights, payment protection, and a liability cap.
Negotiate with the client to adopt Document B for the final project contract.

disclaimer: This is information about the text you provided, not legal advice. It doesn't know your local law, your negotiating position, or anything outside the document, and it can be wrong.
